body: Akre Capital Management; ran FBR Focus Fund, then the Akre Focus Fund from 2009 (John Neff and Chris Cerrone later took over; Akre stepped back from the strategy around 2020). Returns: compounded over ~13% a year since 2009 (Quartr) and top-third rankings vs peers for years; a Substack figure of 15.44% vs 14.22% for the S&P 500 is unverified; Q4 2024 -0.41% vs +2.41% for the S&P. Process edge: the 'three-legged stool' - (1) an extraordinary business with high returns on owners' capital, (2) talented management with integrity who treat shareholders as partners, (3) a long runway to reinvest free cash flow at high returns. When all three exist it is a 'compounding machine' and the job is to sit still. Signature long holds: American Tower, Mastercard, Moody's, O'Reilly Automotive, later KKR and Constellation Software. Structural edge: patient capital and very low turnover, small team. Mistakes: low turnover means sitting through valuation compression (2022 drawdown) and occasional late exits from businesses whose reinvestment runway faded (unverified specifics). Copyable: the three questions are a direct checklist for Indian compounders (e.g., ROE >20%, honest promoter, reinvestment runway); hold winners; measure in 5-year blocks.
title: Chuck Akre - the three-legged stool compounder approach

body: Mumbai investor behind Param Capital. Public holdings (>1% stakes): ~72-73 stocks as of early 2026; portfolio value estimates range from ~Rs 6,163 crore to ~Rs 7,373 crore depending on date and source. Largest disclosed holdings in Dec 2025 data: Neuland Laboratories (~Rs 496.5 crore) and Radico Khaitan (~Rs 379.4 crore). Q1 FY26 fresh buys included Valor Estate (6.5m shares, ~Rs 120.6 crore), J&K Bank, Wendt India, Tatva Chintan and Yatharth Hospital. Sector spread: pharma/CDMO, infrastructure, chemicals, textiles, alcobev. Edge: structural - large capital spread across many mid/small names, ability to take block and pre-IPO/QIP allocations; process (as reported) - blends earnings-growth/turnaround picks with momentum, actively adds and exits. Track record: no published return series; net-worth figures in media are aggregator estimates (single-source). Mistakes: specific losses are not documented in sources found; like other superstar books, many small positions have suffered 40-60% falls in smallcap drawdowns. Copyable: his top holdings illustrate a useful pattern - turnarounds that became re-rated compounders (Neuland's CDMO shift, Radico's premiumisation) - but the quarterly-lagged, >1%-only disclosure makes ticker-cloning unreliable.
title: Mukul Agrawal - Param Capital, active multi-stock smallcap book (India)
